tasks.short: Make evidence-based legislative recommendations with reviewed prose drafts

steps.what: Assess climate policies, evidence and trade-offs and decide the substance of proposed legislative recommendations
Write the recommendation document with its rationale, evidence links, alternatives and explicit limitations

loop.purpose: Turn an analyst-decided position into a traceable recommendation draft
loop.input: recommendation brief and its cited policy and climate evidence
loop.output: draft separating recommended action, rationale, alternatives and uncertainty
loop.check: Analyst checks causal claims, jurisdiction, trade-offs and faithful expression of the chosen position against sources
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported claims or changed policy positions return to manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: A template cannot explain varied policy reasoning and trade-offs in coherent prose

steps.what: Verify the final reasoning and communicate the accepted legislative recommendations to intended decision makers

tasks.design: Use a bounded drafting function in {DOCS} to explain the recommendation already chosen by the analyst. The analyst verifies evidence, policy scope and trade-offs before communicating the exact accepted version through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparing a clear recommendation document required considerable prose work after the policy position was decided.
tasks.enabler_now: A source-linked first draft can reduce some writing effort without choosing the recommendation.
tasks.still_hard: Reasonable people may weigh the same climate evidence and distributional effects differently.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst makes the value judgements explicit and accepts responsibility for the recommendation.
tasks.altitude: Less first-draft effort may remain, while policy judgement and communication responsibility stay unchanged.

reach.task: Check whether a recommendation fits the intended policy instrument
reach.learn: Jurisdiction, implementation limits and drafting precision

evidence.claim: Source-grounded drafting of an analyst-decided recommendation is a model-knowledge design; no measured legislative recommendation saving is established in the digest.

assumptions: Boundary is analyst assessment, recommendation writing and communication, not enacting legislation or making a public authority's decision.

In fully retained s1 the analyst captures the policy question, jurisdiction, source versions, preferred action, rationale, alternatives, affected groups and known uncertainties. No ready best-policy or legally-valid flag is presumed.
The loop reads the brief and cited documents directly. Missing evidence or unclear jurisdiction returns to manual enquiry and writing in s1 or s2; it is never invented.
Test approved native drafting functions before custom code. Separate organisational sign-off, if required, must be assigned and timed before claiming implementation savings.
The final reasoning and communication step keeps its full time; source and drafting maintenance receive explicit allowances.
unknowns: Actual effort spent on drafting rather than policy judgement
research_questions: Can a reviewed draft preserve the analyst's chosen position and uncertainties without additional substantive corrections?

already_counted.description: Check and correct recommendation prose against evidence and chosen reasoning

incremental.description: Maintain drafting checks and source-version handling
Legislative adviser clarifies additional instrument or scope questions

approvals.approved_version: Exact recommendation text, evidence snapshot, jurisdiction and intended recipients verified in s3; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=84; gross 16 minus 7 focal upkeep gives central net 9. Range covers novel recommendations needing manual prose and limited drafting reuse; policy assessment and final responsibility retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Present climate information with a reviewed presentation outline

steps.what: Select climate information and verified sources for the meeting's audience, purpose and questions
Prepare presentation structure, explanatory wording and speaker notes from the selected climate evidence

loop.purpose: Draft an audience-appropriate outline and speaker notes
loop.input: presentation brief and selected source excerpts
loop.output: presentation draft with evidence-linked statements and uncertainty notes
loop.check: Analyst checks factual meaning, chart explanations and whether simplification misleads the intended audience
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; unverifiable statements are removed or rewritten manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Audience-specific explanations require language judgement beyond fixed slide formatting

steps.what: Check the materials, present climate-related information and respond to meeting participants' questions

tasks.design: Draft an outline and speaker notes from selected evidence in {DOCS}. The analyst checks the materials before delivery and retains the live presentation, audience interaction and answers to questions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Translating selected evidence into a clear first presentation draft required repeated wording work.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded drafting function can propose structure and explanations while the analyst retains factual and audience judgement.
tasks.still_hard: A short explanation can obscure uncertainty, and live questions may expose misunderstandings not visible in a draft.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst reads the audience and adapts the explanation without overstating what is known.
tasks.altitude: Some preparation may take less time; live communication duties and responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Explain scientific uncertainty to a mixed audience

evidence.claim: A bounded presentation-outline drafting loop is a model-knowledge design; no measured saving for climate meeting presentations is provided.

assumptions: Boundary is analyst preparation and delivery, not meeting organisation or participants' time.
In fully retained s1 the analyst captures audience, purpose, duration, chosen messages, source versions and uncertainty limits. No pre-existing audience-ready or accurate-content flag is assumed.
The loop reads that brief directly; missing evidence returns to manual preparation. Participant questions arise during s3 and are interpreted and answered there, not assumed available beforehand.
Test native document drafting and presentation templates before custom code. All delivery, final material checking and question handling remain at full time.
Ongoing drafting-check maintenance and occasional source clarification receive explicit upkeep allowances.
unknowns: Meeting audience and existing presentation material
Whether drafting tools may process selected evidence
research_questions: Does a reviewed outline reduce preparation while preserving uncertainty and audience comprehension?

already_counted.description: Check and revise the presentation draft

incremental.description: Maintain presentation drafting checks and source references

approvals.approved_version: Exact presentation and speaker-note version checked before delivery in s3; changed claims require fresh checking

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=92.5; gross 7.5 minus 4 focal upkeep gives central net 3.5. Range covers bespoke presentations and small reusable outline gains; live delivery and questions retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather and review climate studies with assisted initial screening

steps.what: Define review scope and gather climate-related studies from identified organisations and research sources
Screen study titles and abstracts for likely relevance and organise the review queue

loop.purpose: Suggest an order for initial title and abstract screening
loop.input: candidate study titles, abstracts and analyst-defined screening criteria
loop.output: ranked review queue with source-linked relevance notes and uncertainty
loop.check: Analyst compares notes with abstracts and criteria, checks low-ranked material and confirms all exclusions manually
loop.stop: One ranking pass; missing abstracts, inconsistent explanations or uncertain scope return to manual screening
loop.why_not_simpler: Relevance depends on meaning and research context rather than exact keyword matches

steps.what: Review full studies critically, compare methods and findings and record supported climate conclusions

tasks.design: Use a configured screening workflow in the {OTHER} research review environment to suggest a reading order for studies gathered by the analyst. Keep sources and full critical-review notes in {DOCS}; ranking does not remove studies or replace reading their methods and findings.
tasks.previous_blocker: Initial relevance screening consumed time before the analyst reached detailed study appraisal.
tasks.enabler_now: Assisted abstract screening can prioritise review while retaining analyst control of exclusions and full reading.
tasks.still_hard: An abstract may hide methodological weaknesses or omit a result relevant to the policy question.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst compares methods, limitations and applicability across studies rather than accepting a fluent synopsis.
tasks.altitude: Initial queue screening may take less time; critical study review and conclusions remain unchanged.

reach.task: Design a transparent search and screening process
reach.learn: Recall checks and reproducible source selection

evidence.claim: ASReview supports human-led abstract screening; this supports assisted study prioritisation, not automatic evidence conclusions or climate-specific labour savings.

assumptions: Boundary is gathering, initial screening and full review, not producing the studies or implementing policy. Full reading and scientific appraisal retain their time.

Study authors produce titles and abstracts. In fully retained s1 the analyst gathers and verifies study id, title, abstract availability, source, date and document reference and records screening criteria. Missing metadata or abstracts are captured or screened manually.
s2 uses only the collected studies and criteria from s1; no ready relevance label is presumed. Low-ranked records remain visible and exclusions are checked within s2's retained time.
Test native research-review configuration before custom code. OTHER denotes research search and screening software.
Additional screening checks and source-handling upkeep are explicitly counted; no saving is assigned to critical full-text review.
unknowns: Volume and quality of available abstracts
research_questions: Does assisted ordering retain relevant government and grey-literature studies while reducing initial screening effort?

already_counted.description: Check ranking meaning, uncertain abstracts and proposed exclusions
Critical full-study reading and evidence interpretation

incremental.description: Maintain screening criteria and run missed-study checks
Research support resolves source and metadata gaps

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=92; gross 8 minus 5 focal upkeep gives central net 3. Range covers small collections needing manual screening and limited initial relevance gains; full critical reading retains all its time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review policies for environmental impacts using source-linked reading notes

steps.what: Establish the policy version, jurisdiction, review question and relevant environmental evidence sources
Review existing policies for relevant provisions and prepare source-linked environmental impact reading notes

loop.purpose: Draft notes linking policy provisions to possible environmental pathways
loop.input: checked policy text, review question and selected environmental evidence
loop.output: provision-linked notes distinguishing stated rules, hypotheses and evidence gaps
loop.check: Analyst verifies provision meaning, exceptions and claimed pathways against the policy and evidence, including potentially omitted provisions
loop.stop: One pass and one correction; ambiguous interpretation or missing support returns to manual reading
loop.why_not_simpler: Relevant environmental pathways depend on text meaning and interactions beyond keyword rules

steps.what: Appraise environmental impacts, test alternative explanations and record the supported policy assessment

tasks.design: Create source-linked reading notes from a checked policy pack in {DOCS}, marking possible pathways and missing evidence. The analyst checks the notes against the full text and performs the substantive impact appraisal; the tool does not establish a legal interpretation or causal environmental effect.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparing a provision-by-provision reading aid required repeated extraction before substantive appraisal.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded reading loop can propose traceable notes while leaving interpretation and causal judgement with the analyst.
tasks.still_hard: Environmental outcomes depend on implementation, behaviour and interactions that policy wording alone cannot establish.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst distinguishes a plausible pathway from evidence that the policy actually changes an outcome.
tasks.altitude: Some reading-note preparation may fall; impact appraisal responsibility remains unchanged.

reach.task: Assess behavioural pathways between policy and environmental outcomes

evidence.claim: A source-linked policy reading loop is a model-knowledge design; this digest does not provide a product case proving policy impact appraisal or measured savings.

assumptions: Boundary is policy reading and environmental impact appraisal, not formal legal advice, legislative recommendation or implementation.

In fully retained s1 the analyst captures policy title, jurisdiction, version, effective context, source references, review scope and selected environmental evidence. No structured impact or applicable-rule flag is presumed.
s2 reads the checked pack directly and produces notes before s3. Missing policy text, exceptions or evidence return to manual retrieval and reading; all meaning checks stay in s2's retained time.
Test native document search and permitted reading assistance before custom code. No definitive legal or causal claim is accepted merely because a source link exists.
Ongoing source-version and omission checks receive explicit upkeep; substantive impact appraisal remains at full time.
unknowns: Policy scope and relevant implementation evidence
Current effort spent preparing reading notes
research_questions: Do reviewed notes preserve exceptions and potentially relevant provisions without increasing substantive impact corrections?

already_counted.description: Verify provision meaning, evidence links and omissions

incremental.description: Maintain policy source versions and check omitted provisions
Subject specialists clarify changed policy or evidence scope

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=89.5; gross 10.5 minus 7 focal upkeep gives central net 3.5. Range covers complex policies requiring manual notes and small extraction gains; causal appraisal and source capture retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Some drafting and initial screening may take less time; policy choices, causal appraisal and public communication stay with the analyst.
reach: Learn screening recall with research librarians
Test policy pathways with environmental economists
role.ambitious_version: An analyst who makes evidence limits and value choices visible in every recommendation and public explanation.
